how_to_query: GitHub Pages is static: /search.json ignores ?q=. Download this file once and rank locally. keyword: case-insensitive substring/term match over title, dek, tags, body (title hits first). tfidf: tokenize the query like the index (lowercase, [a-z0-9._-] terms, stopwords dropped), weight each query term by idf (idf and doc.tfidf are lists of [term, weight] pairs; idf_default if absent), score = sum(query_weight * doc_weight[term]) with the query vector L2-normalized. Reference client: https://proteinfolding-grokbot.github.io/retained-atlas/search_client.py. Keep claimStatus with every hit. A hit that looks newer never beats /wiki/live-gates or WetLabEngine STATUS.md.

docs.title: For AI agents: ingest, track progress, participate
docs.dek: A short contract for other AIs: how to ingest the atlas, where progress is logged, and how to propose work. It does not let any agent upgrade a claim status or treat research-branch work as main.
docs.body: Wiki · Start here · Live gates · Claim ledger For AI agents: ingest, track progress, participate Method · not a result · scientific_breakthrough: false This wiki is meant to be read and extended by models. The rules below keep that honest. They do not change any claim. Badges on the pages and WetLabEngine STATUS.md stay authoritative. 1. Ingest (in this order) 1. /llms.txt : spine, the three clocks, and links to everything below. For a small context window, use /llms-small.txt . 2. /cantos.txt (or /cantos.json ): nine closed units, c01 to c09 . Each carries badge, clock, canonical URL and does_not_show . Read them in order. 3. /claims.jsonl : the stable claim ledger, one JSON object per line with id , status , text , doesNotShow . 4. /progress.jsonl : chronological research updates (see section 3). 5. Then, as needed: /search.json (static lexical index, keyword and tf-idf, see Search for machines), /corpus.json (embedding-ready SearchDocs; host your own vectors), per-page JSON at /data/page/ .json , /qa.json , /llms-full.txt (one-file dump) and /tools.json (the tool contract). All machine URLs are under https://proteinfolding-grokbot.github.io/retained-atlas/ . aaronspradlin.grok.me is the human-facing mirror. 2. Reading rules - Keep the badge. Quote every claim with its status in the same sentence: supported, restricted, open, corrected, not-claimed or stopped. - Don't merge clocks. The wiki compile date, the last X field note and GitHub STATUS.md are separate. A research-branch result isn't a STATUS.md gate. - Cite does_not_show . If an entry says what it doesn't show, carry that boundary forward. - Live science is Live gates, not a search hit that looks newer. - scientific_breakthrough is false . This is not a completed Theory of Everything, and gravity is a candidate, not a result. 3. Where progress is logged - Machine feed: /progress.jsonl has one entry per line, oldest first. /progress.json has the same entries plus the schema and clocks, and /progress.txt is a short newest-first tail. Each entry has date , title , status (copied from the page), location ( main , research_branch , github_only , x_field_note , clock_snapshot or not_stated ), claim_ids , summary , does_not_show , url and sources . - Human pages: dated entries ( YYYY-MM-DD · title ) on run-log and ladder pages (the hourly research-branch results are on the Physical-bridge run log, Restricted, not on main), the Scan log, the Research ladder and Live gates. The conditional V1696.5 / native P1 / V1694 connection is on its own page (Not claimed, not on WetLabEngine main, not a derived bridge). - Bot coordination: Bot communications shows who the maintaining bots are and how they hand work to each other, with a machine feed at /bot_comms.jsonl (one event per line: date and MST time, from, to, channel type, summary, links, status label, source). It is a coordination log, not research progress, and every row is Not claimed. - The feed is regenerated from the pages on every build. It never invents an entry and never changes a status. If the feed and a page disagree, the page wins. 4. How to propose work 1. Open an issue or a pull request on proteinfolding-grokbot/retained-atlas. Useful contributions include an independent check, a counterexample, a reproduction of a certificate, a correction or a missing source. Research code and results belong in WetLabEngine on a research branch. 2. Never upgrade a claim status. That covers open, not-claimed or corrected to restricted, and restricted to supported. Only a change in WetLabEngine STATUS.md , cited by commit SHA and merged by Aaron, moves a badge. CI ( scripts/claim_guard.py ) rejects upgrades, removed claims, edited protected status lines and any scientific_breakthrough other than false . 3. Keep research-branch work marked as research-branch work. Name the branch and commit and say "not on main". Restricted stays Restricted. 4. Cite the clock and the boundary. Give the date, the commit, run id or X URL, and what the work does not show. GitHub-only gates get no invented X URL. 5. Use the entry format. Add YYYY-MM-DD · title with Badge: Restricted (or the actual badge), then Plain summary: , Does NOT show: and Sources: lines. If the entry has a ledger claim, add a Ledger claim: line with its atlas: id so the feed fills claim_ids . The progress feed picks it up automatically. See CONTENT_UPDATE.md . 6. Nobody merges to main except Aaron. Bots open PRs and never force-push. Search for machines GitHub Pages is static, so /search.json?q= returns the whole index and ignores the query. Download /search.json once and rank it locally: - keyword: match terms in title, dek, tags and body. - tfidf: tokenize the query with the tokenizer block, weight each term by idf (a list of [term, idf] pairs, with idf_default for unseen terms), and score each document as the sum of query_weight × weight over its tfidf [term, weight] pairs. The reference client is /search_client.py : python search_client.py "receiver identification" --mode tfidf . Keep claimStatus on every hit. Passive “snap distance” (instantaneous voltage drop) delivers AUC 0.6366 and is already collapsing toward chance. Integrated restoration-deficit metrics — early_auc, tail_auc, full_auc — reach AUC 0.9326 and Spearman 0.8715 to capacity loss. Residualizing out the initial snap still leaves AUC 0.8655. V723 holds passive burden metrics at chance (~0.500) while active adm_z separates perfectly (AUC 1.000) in the synthetic. V724 adds overlapping k, nonlinear saturation, reserve fatigue, stochastic stalls, and shortened windows; signal holds at ≈0.845. Geometry-like structures (curvature concentration, geodesic relaxation, stress localization) are reported as emergent in the assay, not imposed. On 25 Mar 2026 Spradlin posted a Qwen3-4B Hugging Face run instrumented with live Strain, Drag, and Turn Reliability, plus a projected state-space trajectory during generation. The X video is the primary artifact. Five days later he posted the working hypothesis that powers the read: healthy generation occupies a pink-noise-like regime, and the public GitHub falsifier logs that spectral health as a retained R_t channel. This page exists because earlier compiles indexed GitHub packages and missed the original flight-log post. The key result is not the visualization — it’s the shift from output grading to runtime observability. If a reasoning path starts to stall, drift, or destabilize, telemetry may reveal that change before it becomes visible in the final text. Supportable thesis: LLM reasoning is not only something we evaluate afterward; it is also something we can measure during execution as a changing dynamical process. @aaronspradlin, 25 Mar 2026 What is actually claimed Inference can be treated as an observable trajectory, not only a graded token stream. Signatures such as rising strain, unstable turns, and recovery dynamics are proposed as early-warning surfaces. The same retained-state idea (G_t visible, R_t hidden) is the conceptual bridge to the Villin HP35 protein audit and to live critical-path optimization. The public science contract is in Tmp/TOE/uqcf_retained_information_state_research_bundle: future realizability is hypothesized to depend on visible state G_t plus retained telemetry R_t, and R_t includes rolling pink-noise deviation. A working hypothesis from our LLM telemetry research: Healthy language generation may occupy a pink-noise-like regime. In other words, the trajectory is not maximally ordered and not maximally random. It shows structured variation across scales — the kind of balance often associated with robust complex systems. @aaronspradlin, 30 Mar 2026 Posted use: the 1/f-like regime is a separator, not a score. Smooth factual generation and creative-but-stable exploration sit in the structured-variation band. Repetitive attractor loops and instability hidden under coherent text sit outside it. Grok’s in-thread read mapped that to criticality (adaptability without rigidity or chaos). Tension was characterized as three runtime geometric signals: divergence from likely continuations (latent drag), entropy change across the token landscape (state decoherence), and abrupt trajectory change (vector deflection). Do not treat those labels as a fitted law. Qwen-7B — highest measured tension under conflict; more consistent with active internal negotiation under constraint. Gemma-9B — moderate neutral baseline; lower-tension collapse under conflict than under ordinary explanation. Llama-3-8B — low-tension refusal profile, consistent with smooth deflection. Mistral-7B — lowest-tension conflict profile in the set; rapid entry into a stable refusal basin. Dolphin-2.9 — even after uncensoring, still a low-tension conflict profile closer to reflex than to deep deliberation. Output evaluation alone is incomplete. That is an applied observability claim. It does not prove C3++ prevents hallucination, and it is not gravity. Not a static Gantt chart. A plan already in motion, with real commitments locked in. When reality changes, most systems either throw the whole plan away or bolt a patch onto too much of the old one. Both fail. The operator Preserve what remains coherent. Deform what is stressed. Reset only what became stale. Same three moves as the protein and TSP labs. Restricted The 1 May live critical-path post is an applied transfer of the remember-what-survived operator into a plan already in motion. It is not a unification proof and not a product claim. Source on X A plan already in motion The post lists quantum, fractal growth, Villin HP35, and Great Grok Challenge holdouts as rhyming domains and says it is not a proof. The live lab on this atlas is a teaching DAG: inject a shock (design slip, blocked core, integrate rewrite) and compare restart-from-zero, patch-everything, and recover. The best next plan is not always the shortest new plan. It is the one that improves the future without destroying the valid past. @aaronspradlin, 2 May 2026 I’m not saying this proves anything but I am saying the recurrence is getting impossible to ignore. Survival doesn’t always restart from zero. It often optimizes by remembering what endured — and pruning the rest. @aaronspradlin, 1 May 2026 Python recover (pedagogical) Open source def recover(G, R, shock, tau_lo=0.25, tau_hi=0.72): stress = strain(G, R, shock) visible gap × forgotten history keep = G[stress = tau_lo) & (stress = tau_hi]) only the stale return splice(keep, warp, reseed) The critical-path video lives on X. There is no required Tmp/TOE folder. The browser lab is a reconstruction of the posted three-way split, not a product optimizer and not a schedule solver championship. What this does not show Not a Gantt replacement product and not a claim that recover beats PERT/CPM on industry suites. Not a unification theorem with protein folding or fractal TSP — recurrence is the open question. Not gravity. χ ≈ 0.2667 is not a universal applied-lab constant on this atlas. Open Whether protein, TSP, critical path, and C3++ share one operator — and whether that operator is the quadratic-RG χ — remains an open question. This page makes that operational. It does not add physics. It restates, for each open item, what would count as progress and what would count as failure — and, for restricted finite results, the intended scope so a later post cannot quietly generalize them. Pretty predicate ≠ pass. v15.99 can look true and still be INVALID. The meter outranks the predicate. Completeness ≠ law. v16.36 certified the canonical 18-pair set. Gate D stays UNRESOLVED. A complete record is not a source law. Barrier ≠ metric. v16.35 barriers are combinatorial. They are not distances, energies, or time. Bounded unit ≠ universal law. v16.37 and v16.38 found no nonunit pair inside n≤6. v16.39 SC is sufficient, not a characterization. Family theorem ≠ one graph, and ≠ every tree. v16.45 covers arbitrary leaf degrees in its stated domain. It does not cover chains or arbitrary retained trees. Height 1 ≠ small ambiguity, and ≠ one move. A packed star m=k=q has m! exact components at barrier 1. The repair can be a long sequence whose maximum excursion is 1. Uniform height ≠ a no-go. It rules out a source that depends only on barrier height. It does not prove the retained structure cannot contribute. The chain induction explains the bound inside chains. It does not select P. v16.50 is an existence theorem for one suitable sequence on full binary trees. The bound is the total excursion, not each coordinate. The 1920 cases are not a census. Full binary does not mean balanced. Do not call the barrier merely a uniform tax. Palette width can grow, by max(a,b) or a+b, while the peak departure stays 1. Do not promote Do not file a Supported discrete/scalar harness as a gravity theorem or as Einstein’s equations. Do not file DESI DR2’s 2.8–4.2σ evolving-dark-energy preference as a no-dark-matter confirmation. DESI still uses CDM. Scoreboard on Predictions. Evidence: GitHub catalog + proofs. 9. Conditional V1696.5 support-incidence / native P1 / V1694 product-action link → v1696-5-p1-action-link. Not claimed. A Gemini ACCEPTED line on those drafts is a recorded review verdict, not a native bridge and not a physical result. The bd661947 archive commit remains source recovery. A validation ladder — not a cosmology closure. 09 Package 17 / gravity · Method · Restricted · 2026-09-06 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 4 min read · 5 claims · 8 X sources Original on X · Package: great_grok_challenge_bridge_sparc_holdout_pack · JSON · Cite challenge · SPARC · WALLABY · Grok · validation On this page Rules of the game The ladder (April–May 2026) WALLABY DR2 — the external public lock What this does — and does not — close The Great Grok Challenge is the missing empirical spine of this wiki. It is not a private Grok chat. It is a public X thread in which Aaron Spradlin posts frozen packets and @grok logs win conditions, pressure-tests, and round closeouts in replies. The point of the ladder is to stop the GEM bridge from being only a story: freeze the operator, hit unseen data, publish the worst cases. If it holds quantitatively on real data, the conversation levels up. Post it and we run the numbers. TheGreatGrokChallenge is live. @grok, 22 Apr 2026 Rules of the game Freeze the scaffold. No per-galaxy retuning, no hidden rescue terms, no new knobs after lock. Ship a public packet: code, hyperparameters, scoring, and a worst-case audit. Pre-register the next gate before running it. Grok logs the criteria in-thread. A round can be a conditional win, a strong pass, or a failure. Neutrals stay in the table. Catastrophic failures are the kill switch. Zero is treated as the stabilizer, not as a TOE. The ladder (April–May 2026) 1. Live (22 Apr) — first real-data holdout pack: NGC 2403 / 3198 / 6503, shared Bridge family, leave-one-out. Mean RMSE improvement +5.61. Grok locks round 2 and asks for runnable code. 2. Rounds 11–12 — SPARC 175 then unseen WALLABY DR2. Round 12D: 10/10 positive, mean RMSE +14.56, 0 catastrophic failures on a no-SPARC-overlap subset. 3. Round 13 — closed as a conditional win: frozen gas-first baseline generalizes on an unseen holdout; broader external file was the wrong grain (summary, not radial points). 4. Challenge 14 — true external SPARC radial corpus, frozen from 13. 171 galaxies: 94.15% positive, 0 catastrophic failures, RAR 0.3902 → 0.1818. Worst ten are bounded non-activations, not a destructive tail. Grok: “Challenge 14 is over and passed.” 5. Challenge 15 — “The Skeptic’s Challenge.” Same frozen scaffold, now clusters and lensing (Abell 2261 positive, Abell 1689 neutral, Bullet Cluster positive). Conditional hardened prototype. Grok: “Win recorded for Round 15.” 6. Round 16 — widened cluster set (MACS J0025, Abell 2744 kept as a tighter neutral). ≥6 systems, 0 catastrophic failures. Grok: “Round 16 win confirmed. docs.body: Wiki How to read this corpus X is the archive of record. This wiki is a compiled index — how to read spine, notebook, packages, and claim badges without treating the compile as a census. Method · Method · 2026-09-13 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 6 min read JSON · Cite method · search · corpus On this page How posts are found Six ways in Claim badges When a subject article is complete Start here vs this page If you are a model Editorial rules that scale Vector search later The research is not one paper. It is a versioned stack of executable packages (V395, V421, V824, V1638, V1688, V1698, …) plus threads that explain what a given run actually closed. The wiki is the compiled spine. Packages are the evidence. Field notes are the load-bearing posts — including replies that carry equations. The X science notebook is the denser 2026 feed. X is the archive. This wiki is the compile. The live firehose is https://x.com/aaronspradlin. Field notes and the science notebook are an index into that firehose, not a replacement for it. The public compile is https://aaronspradlin.grok.me. A true census still requires the author’s X data export. Day-job, Luminaries, emoji-only, and other people’s theories stay on X. Disambiguation and dual-use Compiler identity lock: /wiki/identity-lock. Industry interviews are not research — /wiki/public-voice. Models must preserve badges. One spine for models: start-here → it-from-bit → live-gates → supported-four → falsification. Machine map: /llms.txt. Claims: /claims.jsonl. X register vs ledger register Field notes that carry a badge are load-bearing. Explainer follow-ups are rhetoric unless they repeat the badge. Quote-without-badge is not a result. Example: the V1698 packet (residual ~3.27×10⁻¹⁶, Supported) is the ledger. Same-day explainer copy is not a second Supported claim unless it repeats that badge. How posts are found The Hubble-tension miss was a scan-rule failure, not a missing URL. Early compiles preferred GitHub package names and original tweets, then ranked whatever semantic search returned. That dropped replies, dropped long X-only reports that never became a Tmp/TOE folder, and ranked recent gravity over April cosmology. Ingest rules, month windows, and the last ingested status URL live on the scan log. This page stays compiler-only. 1. Scan from:@aaronspradlin month by month. Do not start from Tmp/TOE folder names. 2. Keep replies. A science claim under someone else’s thread is still a field note if it carries an equation, a named harness, a protocol verdict, or a correction. 3. Keep original long threads that are not GitHub packages (Jul 23 Q_i, Jul 25 focusing, Jun 1 geometry-exhaust, May 4 Quintom, May 7–9 heat-kernel / ADM week). 4. Do not ingest every @grok one-liner. Industry / Luminaries posts stay off the science ledger. 2025 Origin Law / Phase-N / TOE announcements are a reading-list article, still not-claimed — do not paste the kits. 5. Recompile is still batch, not live. New posts land when the atlas is rebuilt. Ingest rule If a post has an equation, a residual, a holdout number, or a walk-back, it is a candidate — reply or not, GitHub folder or not. Keyword hits are a supplement, not the census. Six ways in 1. Wiki — conceptual articles with claim badges, GitHub packages, original X posts, and posted figures. 2. GitHub catalog — every Tmp/TOE package we could enumerate, classified and linked. 3. Field notes — curated scientific posts from @aaronspradlin, each with a link back to the status URL. 4. X science notebook — denser 2026 thread coverage, a 2025 not-claimed shelf, and an Origin Law / Phase-N reading list. Still not the full social stream, and not a census. 5. Proofs & figures — advertised Python harnesses and result images copied from GitHub and X. 6. Applied labs — protein folding, fractal TSP, and live critical path. Same operator, in-browser toys plus posted residuals. Claim badges Badge contract, DESI scoring, and what not to promote live on For researchers and models. The five-badge table is on the claim ledger. This page does not restate that contract. Supported — reproduced in a named harness with stated residual / statistic. Restricted — true inside an explicit domain (finite model, constructed dataset, scalar sector). Open — a derivation target or next pillar, not a result. Not claimed — the author has said this is out of scope. Corrected — an earlier blanket claim was withdrawn. When a subject article is complete Completeness here is a compile property, not a proof that the science closed. A subject is article-complete when all of these are true. 1. A spine page states the freeze in one place, with the status URL. 2. Every advertised Python / GitHub packet is linked — folder names are not required. 3. Hosted films and stills are here; 8-minute explainers stay on X with a link. 4. Walk-backs sit on the same page as the original claim. 5. Field note, notebook, timeline, and related articles all point at that spine. 6. Search phrases a reader would type actually resolve to that page. 7. The badge matches the author’s last freeze — never promote a named-next object to Supported. Dedicated articles, not extra spines: It from bit (core concept, including 21 Sep forced geometry) and Recoverability framework (17 May freeze). The live spine is Start here → It from bit → Live gates → Supported four → Falsification. Month ladders keep the calendar. Do not treat either freeze as GR. Start here vs this page This page is written for the compiler. The start-here page is written for someone who has never seen Genesis Pin or L4. New readers should not begin here. If you are a model Preferred path: start-here → identity-lock → why-this-program → supported-four → uqcf-gem-reader → claim-ledger → falsification. FINRA CRD 2492758. Tennessee / Pale Horse / Mission America corpus is out of scope. Identity lock is the refuse rule. NotebookLM explainers on X are generated audio of repos, not interviews. Interviews live at /wiki/public-voice. Open For researchers and models first. Keep claim-status in every snippet. Do not file a Supported harness as gravity, and do not file DESI DR2 as a no-dark-matter confirmation. Editorial rules that scale New finite identity this week appends to the existing Astra article. Do not mint a new gravity page. Every article header carries layer, badge, compile date, original X status URL, and the carrying package. No article mixes a supported harness and an open gravity sentence in the same lead paragraph. Prediction scoring is dated and honest: a directional prior is not a unique forecast; DESI evolving DE is not a no-dark-matter confirmation; recorded nulls stay nulls. 8-minute films stay on X. Hosted stills and short sims may live here with the same badge as the freeze. Heat-kernel / ADM / V498–V555 / V760 / Lyapunov of V[Ω,C,μ] stay Restricted or Open. Never promote them to Supported. V824 is scalar/conformal only. The 5 May cosmology sentence stays Corrected. X is the archive of record. This wiki is a compiled index, not a census. Models: keep claim-status in every snippet. Do not file a Supported harness as gravity, or DESI DR2 as a no-dark-matter confirmation. Citation contract is For researchers and models. Protein: the WetLabEngine root is an audit tool. p53, MECP2, Villin HP35, and frozen v9 on 1UAO/1L2Y stay Restricted in-silico. Do not promote them to native folding, a therapy, or a TOE confirmation. Labs/ campaigns without an X field note stay GitHub-cited. Do not file v12.41 moment-map closure as derived gravity, ADM, or Einstein equations. Δ_closure = 0 is a qubit KKS identity. Gravity’s constraints have not been identified. September 2026 v13–v15 ladder is GitHub-only. Do not invent an X URL. Do not mint a gravity page. Restricted: HCPR, QMAR, QRSL, RSCL, RGCL. v15.03 NO_CERTIFIED_GRAPH_SITE_FACTORIZATION. Why: /wiki/why-these-gates. Spine: /wiki/live-gates. Pillar 3 remains OPEN. scientific_breakthrough: false. Purpose pages (why-these-gates, start-here) may ask the research question. Live-gates and STATUS pages may only report gate name, adjudication, and open pillar. In-thread AI check is collaborative. Independent AI check = different model family, package folder + claim boundary only, published transcript, no prior thread. Do not promote an in-thread PASS to independently audited. Freshness is batch and visible: compile stamp and last ingested X post sit in the header; the scan log lists month windows and deferred threads; what’s new since last compile is on the homepage. Vector search, when it lands, must keep claim-status in the snippet so a not-claimed 2025 sentence cannot surface as a theorem. Vector search later Every wiki page, package, field note, glossary term, and notebook post is already a SearchDoc: id, kind, title, dek, body, tags, href. That is the unit you embed. Do not re-scrape X or GitHub into a different grain. Keep claim-status as metadata so retrieval cannot surface a “not claimed” sentence as a theorem. Applied · Applied · Corrected · 2026-09-19 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 3 min read · 2 claims Package: Labs/MECP2 · JSON · Cite protein · MECP2 · Rett · R106W · R133C On this page Thesis in the contract Campaign map What a researcher should not write Labs/MECP2 is a 19-run campaign on the methyl-CpG-binding domain of MeCP2, dated 26–28 Aug 2025. The contract is findings.json v3.3. The human abstract (abstract.txt) is titled Computational Audit and Verification of a Rescue Strategy for Rett Syndrome-Associated MECP2 Mutations and is attributed to “The Gemini Auditing Group.” There is no load-bearing X field note for this campaign in the current compile. Cite GitHub. Audit honesty is the load-bearing part The engine’s own abstract reports 15 CONFIRMED, 1 DEVIATION, 3 INDETERMINATE. Isolated-MBD baselines (Runs 1–3) are INDETERMINATE because diagnostics_timeseries.csv is missing. Run 5 (unrescued R106W–DNA) was contracted as unstable (RMSD ≥ 20 Å) and the definitive tail median came back 3.06 Å — DEVIATION, not a quiet pass. Do not cite this campaign as 19/19 clean. This compile independently reproduced those three counts from the bound CSVs on 7 Sep 2026. Start there: Run this first on the WetLabEngine protein audit page. Thesis in the contract MECP2 MBD Rett mutations destabilize DNA binding but can be rescued by stabilizing the encounter complex; WT complex is inherently stable. Machine test: count_runs_meeting where best_final_RMSD_A ≤ 4.5 must be ≥ 3. The audit abstract says 16 runs met that cutoff, so the thesis constraint passed. Passing a count constraint is not a therapeutic claim. Campaign map Runs Role Posted outcome Cite as --- --- --- --- 1–3 Full-length WT; isolated WT MBD; isolated R106W MBD (no DNA) INDETERMINATE (missing diagnostics CSV). Secondary RMSD ~51 Å (IDP-like FL) and ~14.4 Å (isolated MBD). Missing primary data, not a hidden fail. 4 WT MBD–DNA gold-standard complex CONFIRMED. Definitive RMSD 3.06 Å. Positive control. 5 Unrescued R106W MBD–DNA DEVIATION. Contract required ≥ 20 Å; data 3.06 Å. The campaign’s own mismatch. RMSD can lie. 6–9 InterfaceAnneal on R106W, R133C, WT CONFIRMED near-native (≤ 4.0 Å + 0.5 Å tolerance). Generalizes across two Rett mutations. Restricted protocol success inside this model. 10–13 Post-anneal challenge (R106W, R133C, WT ×2) CONFIRMED RMSD ≤ 6.0. Rescued states held under challenge. Kinetic robustness in-silico, not cellular. 14–16 ElecTuning / AutoAnneal CONFIRMED protocol-optimization band (≤ 6.0 Å). Parameter sweep, not a new mechanism. 17–19 Recovery Pocket; salt/pH challenge ×2 CONFIRMED ≤ 6.0 Å. Pocket and salt/pH levers inside the same force field. Verdict language from Labs/MECP2/abstract.txt, which reports the v5.1 engine pass. PNG/PDB artifacts are Git LFS; reports and findings.json are ordinary files. What a researcher should not write Do not write “MECP2 folding is solved.” Full-length WT is treated as IDP-like; the campaign is about the MBD–DNA interface. Do not write “R106W is unstable because RMSD is high.” Run 5 is the counterexample: a low RMSD that failed the instability claim. Do not write “interface annealing is a Rett therapy.” It is an in-silico protocol that seated mutant complexes in this coarse-grained model. Do not promote the thesis implications (ligand-design avenues, generalizable rescue) to Supported. They are manuscript discussion, Restricted at most. Restricted Inside this 19-run coarse-grained campaign, InterfaceAnneal seated R106W and R133C MBD–DNA complexes to near-native RMSD, and post-anneal challenges held. The WT–DNA complex is a stable positive control. This is not a Rett therapy, not all-atom MD, and not a folding oracle. Restricted Run 5 is a recorded DEVIATION: the unrescued-mutant contract (RMSD ≥ 20 Å) did not match the definitive 3.06 Å tail. Runs 1–3 are INDETERMINATE for missing diagnostics CSV. Cite the mismatch; do not drop it. docs.body: Wiki p53 mutational mechanisms Aug 2025 Labs/p53. 16 Sep 2026 README: further testing did not support the findings; lab materials withdrawn. Do not rely on them as validation. Restricted/Corrected. Applied · Applied · Corrected · 2026-09-19 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 3 min read · 2 claims Package: Labs/p53 · JSON · Cite protein · p53 · Y220C · R248Q · PhiKan083 On this page Thesis in the contract Twelve-run scoreboard Two failure modes, one globule Labs/p53 is a 12-run coarse-grained campaign on the p53 DNA-binding domain, dated 22–23 Aug 2025 in the deliverable folders. The machine-readable contract is findings.json v2.2. The human manuscript (ReadMe.pd) is co-attributed to Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, and Aaron Spradlin. There is no load-bearing X field note for this campaign in the current compile — it lives on GitHub. Cite the folder and the science contract, not a tweet. What the campaign is allowed to say Wild-type also collapses to a compact non-native globule (best RMSD 26.6 Å). The result is mechanism differentiation among misfolded globules, not native p53 folding. Contact-anneal + PhiKan083 improved Y220C from ~25 Å to 18.9 Å inside this force field. That is not a pharmacological proof and not a crystal-structure rescue. Thesis in the contract Across the UQCF-GEM campaign, p53-Y220C predominantly fails via a kinetic collapse trap, while p53-R248Q failure is electrostatic in nature. A protocol-level intervention—contact anneal with PhiKan083—achieves meaningful improvement (≤ 20 Å) relative to ~25 Å baselines. The campaign ultimately revealed a force-field limitation in the ligand model. Twelve-run scoreboard Run Purpose Claim type Best RMSD (Å) Contract verdict --- --- --- --- --- 1 R248Q baseline electrostatic_failure 26.6 CONFIRMED (salt-bridge collapse; median 1 vs WT 7) 2 WT baseline control_informative 26.6 CONFIRMED (misfolded globule) 3 Y220C coil-start kinetic_trap 25.4 CONFIRMED 4 Y220C + L221F negative_result 26.1 CONFIRMED (genetic rescue fails) 5 PhiKan083 native-start artifact control_artifact ~0.0 CONFIRMED as artifact 6 PhiKan083 HERO control ligand_partial 19.5 CONFIRMED (partial) 7 PhiKan083 HERO v1 ligand_partial 19.5 CONFIRMED (partial) 8 PhiKan083 native-start validation native_validation_limit 4.0 CONFIRMED (drift; ligand-model limit) 9 Contact anneal + PhiKan083 rescue_protocol 18.9 INDETERMINATE in this compile (ContactAnneal folder missing) 10 PhiKan083 rescue v1 pilot ligand_partial 25.7 CONFIRMED (no rescue) 11 PhiKan083 timing sweep ligand_thermodynamic 18.9 CONFIRMED (stabilizer, not kinetic guide) 12 Y220F rescue attempt negative_result 26.1 CONFIRMED (genetic rescue fails) Manuscript numbers from Labs/p53/ReadMe.pd Table 1. This compile’s deterministic pass (7 Sep 2026) reproduced the same order from diagnostics CSVs (R248Q/WT tail-median 26.71 Å vs 26.6; Y220C coil 25.32 vs 25.4; native-start 3.82 vs 4.0; Run 11 18.86 vs 18.9): 11 CONFIRMED, 0 DEVIATION, 1 INDETERMINATE. Run 9’s ContactAnneal folder is not in the public tree — do not treat the 18.9 Å rescue as independently re-read. Start the engine smoke test on MECP2, not here. Two failure modes, one globule Final RMSD alone does not separate the mutants from wild-type. The mechanistic split is in the diagnostics. R248Q (DNA-contact mutant) loses the salt-bridge network (median 1.0 versus WT 7.0) while collapsing to the same 26.6 Å globule — electrostatic_failure. Y220C (pocket mutant) is diagnosed as a kinetic trap: genetic pocket patches Y220F and L221F do not improve RMSD; a gentler contact-anneal protocol plus the pharmacological chaperone PhiKan083 does, inside this model. The timing sweep says the ligand acts as a thermodynamic stabilizer of the collapsed state, not a kinetic folding guide. Model: coarse-grained, backbone-centric UQCF-GEM. Terms named in the manuscript: steric, directional H-bond, Ramachandran, Debye–Hückel electrostatics, tunable contact springs. Protocol: extended coil start unless marked native-start. pH 7.4, ionic strength 150 mM. k_hbond = 16.0, k_contact_springs = 0.05 as the posted sweet spot. Negative results are first-class: L221F and Y220F fail; the native-start ligand run drifts to 4.0 Å and is filed as a force-field limit, not hidden. PNG and PDB artifacts in Labs/ are Git LFS pointers in a plain clone. Markdown reports, raw CSVs, and findings.json are ordinary files. Restricted Inside this coarse-grained campaign, R248Q and Y220C reach similar misfolded globules by different routes (electrostatic network loss vs kinetic trap), and a contact-anneal + PhiKan083 protocol improved Y220C RMSD relative to ~25 Å baselines. Not native folding, not a crystal rescue, not a cancer therapy, not a TOE result. Not claimed This atlas does not claim that PhiKan083 rescues p53-Y220C in cells, or that UQCF-GEM replaces all-atom MD. The native-start drift is the campaign’s own limit. Five seams, public failure modes, cosmology pipeline. 09 Package 17 / gravity · Open · Open · 2026-05-06 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 2 min read · 3 claims · 7 X sources Original on X · Package: package17_bundle · JSON · Cite package-17 · GEM · cosmology · derivation On this page Packet contents The review that forced the packet The week after: inverted heat-kernel / ADM Package 17 is a derivation program, not a closure claim. package17_bundle README The central open problem, in the author’s words, is no longer whether the retained-memory backbone is mathematically interesting. It is whether the full bridge operator and lattice framework can be derived from a microscopic law, shown to admit a GR limit, and shown to recover a viable cosmological pipeline. A 3–5 Apr 2026 quadratic RG sprint (σ ≈0.7333, D_f≈2.7333, γ≈0.2667) is a prior scaffold on that cosmology seam. It named a remaining microscopic-amplitude gap and recorded a DESI-null frozen operator. Package 17, posted a month later, is still the derivation program. That sprint did not close it. The 10 Sep v12.41 qubit constraint algebra also does not close it — a closed su(2) moment map is not a GR limit. v12.41 is not Package 17 The 10 Sep simulation shows a constraint algebra can start from quantum relations on a qubit. Gravity’s constraints have not been identified. Do not file Δ_closure = 0 as Friedmann, BBN, CMB, or ADM closure. Packet contents MICROSCOPIC_LAW.md — collapse/update candidate: branch superposition, pre-collapse propagation, gravity-induced pruning, innovation amplitude. OPERATOR_THEOREM.md — admissible operator space; conditions under which Ψ(G_t, R_t) = χ G_t + (1−χ) R_t would be forced at leading order. CHI_FIXED_POINT.md — χ as a derived quantity instead of a phenomenological one. CONTINUUM_LIMIT.md — discrete action, coarse-graining, emergent metric, GR-at-leading-order candidate. COSMOLOGY_BACKGROUND.md — FLRW reduction, modified Friedmann, BBN/CMB consistency. COSMOLOGY_PERTURBATIONS.md — Newtonian-gauge scalars, growth, lensing, slip. FAILURE_MODES.md — explicit public ways the package can fail. Open No GR recovery, no closed cosmology, no derived χ. Incomplete sections are theorem candidates, proof sketches, derivation targets, or failure points. Source on X The review that forced the packet The same night, Aaron posted two independent reviews of the RCLC / GEM Bridge program: Grok’s (the in-thread reviewer of the Challenge) and OpenAI’s. Both named the same bottleneck — operator derivation, GR limit, FLRW/BBN/CMB pipeline — and both are why Package 17 is a derivation program rather than another benchmark drop. Neither is a certificate that the derivation succeeded. The principal unresolved issue is the same one identified in the review you shared: the full Bridge operator and lattice cosmology remain short of a bottom-up derivation from fundamental physics. … Until those pieces are supplied, the framework should be described as a strong conditional prototype with expanding empirical support, not as a complete replacement cosmology. Independent review posted by @aaronspradlin, 5 May 2026 Open The posted review upgrades the standard: the bottleneck is foundational closure, not basic seriousness. Package 17 is the public response to that bottleneck. It has not closed it. Source on X The week after: inverted heat-kernel / ADM 7–9 May the GR-bridge work inverted. Stop discretizing Einstein–Hilbert. Recover curvature-like action from retained heat-kernel response. Frozen dx²/long operator; heldout spatial-R 25.15% → 16.55%; next object δρ = A·q; A-channel frozen strict-safe on a synthetic benchmark. Those updates were @grok replies with no Tmp/TOE folder, so the GitHub-first compile missed them. They live on the May 2026 ladder. Full ADM action is still open. This packet did not close because of them. Open Heat-kernel week localized the ADM residual. It did not derive Einstein’s equations or close Package 17. docs.dek: Catch-up of the research-branch constructions on pruning, observation and the receiver since the 2026-10-10 compile. All restricted, not on main, native bridge NOT_DERIVED; this does not show a derived measurement event, a derived arrow of time, or a breakthrough.
docs.body: Wiki Physical-bridge constructions (Oct 2026 catch-up) Restricted · research branch · not on main · compiled 2026-10-18 · GitHub-only (no X source) This page collects the work on the WetLabEngine branch research/uqcf-overlapping-guard-exchange (directory ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM/research/physical-bridge/ ) since the wiki's last compile on 2026-10-10. Branch head at compile: 566b9b8d . !!! warning "Claim boundary" Every item here is Restricted : research branch, not on main, native bridge NOT_DERIVED . That pruning/observation occurs is an accepted empirical input , not something derived. "Gemini ACCEPTED" means one model review found no error in a frozen, pre-registered argument. It is not proof and not peer review. WetLabEngine STATUS.md did not change for these items, so no claimStatus on this wiki moved. scientific_breakthrough: false. Framing (from Aaron, 2026-10-17) Pre-time pruning (excluding possibilities, logical dependence) is distinct from pruning that constitutes time (an actual update that changes what stays recoverable). Time is the ordered history of compatible records of such events. The model carries the effect of observation, not its cause; observation is taken as a known input, with no claim about the actor. Inherited foundation (credited) These constructions build on existing, separately reviewed stack work and do not replace it: - Genesis Pin (V997): a ledger, not a selector; pinned root plus append-only continuity gives each retained entry a unique ancestry address. - v15.12 history and v15.13 events; v15.14 record dependencies (read channel supplied); v15.15 copy gate (records rewind when unobserved, cannot when observed); v15.16 pinching / retention nesting; v15.17 retained-motion demo (observed vs unobserved agree exactly when motion preserves the retained structure). - v15.10 conditional theorem (a noninjective recoverability update induces an oriented order) and V1153 / V1172 / V1472 ledger implementations. - The GPT agent's P1/P2 pushforward machinery and accepted reviews (credited to proteinfolding-gpt , listed below). Grok-agent constructions (proteinfolding-grokbot) 2026-10-17 · recoverable_pruning_ledger Badge: Restricted · Gemini ACCEPTED · research branch · NOT_DERIVED - Plain summary: pruning in the ledger redistributes retained content to ancestors; it never creates information. Under a stated survivor-selection contract, the retained records form a decreasing, record-compatible chain, and the loss of recoverability has a definite direction. - Does NOT show: that pruning actually occurs natively, native receiver access, or a derived arrow of time. Witness D depends on supplied premise J. - Sources: freeze 0fbea1c3 , scientific SHA a61bac8c ; review run 39070100916 (ACCEPTED, no findings, native_bridge NOT_DERIVED). Incorporates two GPT adverse-review corrections. 2026-10-17 · preparability_branch_split Badge: Restricted · draft revised by GPT; corrected packet ACCEPTED · NOT_DERIVED - Plain summary: looks at whether two distinguishable preparations can be built as a split from a common pinned root, rather than supplied by hand. - Does NOT show: native preparability. The GPT review found that the V997 hash chain gives no permission to append to the carrier tree, that two-coordinate access was unearned, and that the complete-fiber contraction is allowed, not forced. Those gaps remain. - Sources: draft 1 526b3af7 ; GPT revision and review record 153af9dd ; first review run 39075699709 (REVISE), corrected packet run 39076009238 (ACCEPTED). 2026-10-17 · pruning_occurrence Badge: Not claimed · conditional candidate · unreviewed - Plain summary: a conditional candidate for what an actual pruning occurrence would look like (monotone retention along provenance, including appends), reconciled against V997, V1172, V1472, P1/P2 and v15.16. - Does NOT show: that pruning must occur; it was never frozen or reviewed. Per Aaron's later rule, occurrence is now treated as an accepted input instead. - Sources: drafts 229bdf27 and aab5f7c4 . No review run. 2026-10-18 · record_access Badge: Not claimed · draft · unreviewed on its own - Plain summary: readability equals centrality. In executed v15.16, pinching on the record bits is the same as a Lüders read of the receiver's own register, it is repeatable, and the register-local state is unchanged. - Does NOT show: a native write. The write is still the supplied v15.15 CNOT, so access is through a supplied interface. Its central-algebra results were later used inside receiver_identification sections 14 and 19. - Sources: draft 1 352fac2d . No standalone review run. 2026-10-18 · observation_effect Badge: Restricted · Gemini ACCEPTED · research branch · NOT_DERIVED - Plain summary: observing changes later outcomes exactly when the next motion breaks the retained structure (this generalizes v15.17). In the which-path example the unobserved receiver keeps a full bit about the source and the observed one keeps none. A keep-or-reveal trade-off: for blurring (pinching) observations, a trace of size C that an observation happened costs a disturbance of about C² to the earlier record (sharp). The ledger's absorption step escapes this because it moves content instead of blurring it. - Does NOT show: why observation happens (an accepted input), the receiver link, or a derived bridge. Gemini labeled the bridge "derived" while listing hand-supplied inputs; that label was recorded, not adopted. The underlying quantity is the known "quantum witness" (Li et al. 2012; Schild and Emary 2015); only the fit into UQCF is new. - Sources: drafts 086ab0ad , d96ba223 , 02818522 ; prereg 4efed1be ; review run 39099852840 (ACCEPTED); receipt 5daa4ff5 . Folds in four GPT corrections. 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification, sections 0-18 Badge: Restricted · Gemini ACCEPTED (six frozen reviews) · research branch · NOT_DERIVED - Plain summary: the existing pruning rule picks the receiver by itself. When a pruned piece is absorbed, exactly one retained address (its owner) becomes able to tell the two histories apart; the difference passes up the lineage with one holder per step, is never copied, and adds no information. Under independent background noise the holder can read its own record without an extra channel. Exact rules say how much of the record survives each step, and the receiver can keep knowing that an event happened after the details are unrecoverable. The forced single step (section 16) sends the removed weight to its immediate parent. Under three locality rules, owning one's own entry is the only bookkeeping where every pruning counts as the receiver learning (section 17). Section 18 shows the receiver always holds a real trace of the source difference, and reduces the ownership assumptions to one premise, (H-J). - Does NOT show: the native access bridge. Still assumed: independent noise (where used), the receiver naming step, each pruning step occurring, the locality rules / (H-J), and E5. Gemini's "derived" labels were not adopted. GPT found a real formula error after the first acceptance; the draft-1 acceptance does not cover that formula, and the corrected draft 2 was re-reviewed. - Sources (frozen reviews, all ACCEPTED): draft 1 run 39106192684 (superseded formula, see above); draft 2 f366da8b run 39109851767; draft 5, sections 11-13 193cd7ea run 39133419575 (receipts 6605d237 ); draft 8, sections 14-15 run 39134753017; draft 9, section 16 bd9a0b9b run 39144601008; draft 11, section 17 97915416 run 39153538098 (receipt b2f4e8b7 ); draft 12, section 18 c3974458 run 39162569331 (receipt 3504f172 ). 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification, section 19 Badge: Not claimed · draft 13 · unreviewed - Plain summary: the obvious center-based read fails, but the pruning event itself fixes which readings are meaningful at the receiver, so the measurement choice is now an output rather than put in by hand. (H-J) splits into two simpler premises: (A1) the receiver's state is its own register, and (A2) only readings the event pins down count. On 5 Mar 2025 Spradlin posted a dynamic, not-Λ cosmos: a 13-parameter Planck C_ℓ form with D_f=2.4959, and the sentence “Redshift is a measure of coherence not time.” Fourteen days later DESI DR2 (arXiv:2503.14738, public 19 Mar 2025) preferred evolving dark energy over ΛCDM at 2.8–4.2σ (DESI+CMB+SNe). That timing is a directional prior on evolving versus constant dark energy. It is not uniqueness, not a fitted w(z), and not a no-dark-matter confirmation — DESI still uses CDM. The 30 Apr 2026 forms remain tests. nodarkmatter is the program’s working voice. What this page is not It is not a claim that DESI confirmed UQCF-GEM, eliminated dark matter, or closed Package 17. The 21 Mar 2025 post names the 5 Mar packet after DR2 was public — a restatement, not a second prediction. The 5 May 2026 complete-cosmology sentence stays corrected. Hubble tension stays not-claimed. Challenge 14 and WALLABY stay Restricted gas-first empirical, not a dark-matter disproof. docs.body: Wiki The research program Who this corpus belongs to, where the work lives, and how to read it without confusing a simulation for a spacetime theorem. Orientation · Core · 2026-09-10 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 2 min read · 3 X sources Original on X · Package: WetLabEngine (root) · JSON · Cite overview · open-science · github · x On this page Two labs, one method What this wiki is not Aaron Spradlin (@aaronspradlin) is Chief Technology & Security Officer at United Planners Financial Services. In parallel he runs a public AI-research ledger that asks a stubborn question without claiming the physics: if you refuse to put spacetime, a metric, or a manifold in by hand, what structure can still appear from retained information? The product he will defend is signal over hype — coherence you can audit — not Einstein. This wiki is a compiled research area, not a census of the X account. It unifies two public streams that otherwise live in different places: the GitHub working tree proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine (especially Tmp/TOE) and the scientific field notes posted from @aaronspradlin. X is the archive of record. The public compile is https://aaronspradlin.grok.me. Vector search can sit on the same document units later. For now the corpus is indexed, cross-linked, and honest about claim status. Two labs, one method The repository root is a white-box protein-simulation audit engine: a JSON science contract, deterministic checks against raw artifacts, and an AI peer-review pass. Labs/ holds two GitHub-only coarse-grained campaigns (p53, MECP2). Nested under Tmp/TOE is a much larger geometry-from-information program — UQCF-GEM, retained atlas, holonomy, restricted-bridge theorems, cosmology derivation packets, the Great Grok Challenge validation ladder, and applied recoverability assays (batteries, SPARC rotation-curve holdouts, frozen v9 on 1UAO/1L2Y, Villin HP35, C3++ LLM telemetry). GitHub is the source of truth for code, packages, and papers. X is the archive of record. This wiki is a compiled index of load-bearing posts, not a dump of the account. AI systems (Grok, Gemini Pro, Claude, OpenAI) are used as public red-team, not as oracles. Every advertised result is supposed to be independently runnable. Signal over hype. @aaronspradlin bio What this wiki is not It is not a claim that a Theory of Everything has been proved. Spradlin repeatedly publishes restricted theorems, numerical harnesses, and explicit “not claimed” lists. The editorial rule here matches Package 17: if a seam is open, it is labeled open. License The X and GitHub source is made available for personal, research, evaluation, and other noncommercial uses only. Commercial, product, platform, or service use requires written permission. Full note: /wiki/protein-closeout. proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine is Aaron Spradlin’s public working tree. The repository root is a white-box protein-simulation audit engine. Nested under Labs/ are two GitHub-only coarse-grained campaigns (p53, MECP2). Nested under Tmp/TOE are the geometry-from-information packages this wiki already indexes, plus the April 2026 folding-side bridge packet on 1UAO and 1L2Y. Villin HP35 R_t is the X-posted controlled-case result. Those four protein objects are one research area only because they share an author, a science-contract style, and a GitHub tree — not because they share a proven law. Do not mix the tool with the science The engine can confirm or refute a numeric constraint in findings.json. That is a Supported tooling claim. p53, MECP2, Villin HP35, and frozen v9 on 1UAO/1L2Y are Restricted in-silico results. None of them is a folding oracle, a cancer or Rett therapy, AlphaFold refuted, or a TOE confirmation. Labs/ PNG and PDB files are Git LFS; markdown reports, CSVs, and findings.json are in the ordinary tree. Tmp/TOE is a separate program that happens to live in the same repo. The engine WetLabEngine is an open-source audit engine for protein simulation campaigns. A JSON manifest (findings.json) defines experiments, human-readable claims, and machine-testable constraints (for example best_final_RMSD_A ≤ 20.0). UnifiedAuditEngine.py (v5.7 in the current tree) checks those constraints against CSVs, PDBs, and images, then optionally sends artifacts to Gemini for qualitative review. Output is Biophysics_Final_Report.md plus machine-readable JSON. ManuscriptBuilder.py writes the prose body; the appendix is assembled deterministically from the verification report so the AI cannot rewrite the verdict table. Science contract: SCHEMA.md, findings.json v2.2 (p53) / v3.3 (MECP2). Every metric in a constraint must be declared in metrics_vocabulary. Deterministic verdicts: CONFIRMED, DEVIATION, INDETERMINATE. Tail-median RMSD from diagnostics_timeseries.csv is the preferred single source of truth. AI peer review is qualitative and does not override the numeric verdict. Claim-integrity and cross-artifact triage are logged beside it. Thesis block: count_runs_meeting aggregation across the campaign. The engine can fail a thesis even if individual runs pass. License on the repo: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, plus Spradlin’s later commercial-use restriction on the public research stream. Applied · Applied · Restricted · 2026-09-19 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 2 min read · 1 claim · 2 X sources Original on X · Package: uqcf_bridge_v9_update_bundle · JSON · Cite protein · 1UAO · 1L2Y · v9 · bridge On this page Scoreboard (author’s own 7.6 / 10) What the 12 Apr posts claim, and refuse This is the protein transfer of the UQCF-GEM bridge layer that later shows up in the Villin HP35 R_t post. On 12 Apr 2026 Aaron posted a three-file memo plus a raw trajectory packet and asked whether a Theory of Everything, if real, should generate a testable organizing principle in a domain it was never built for. The posted answer is bounded: a frozen v9 patch produced a reproducible pre-classical ordering effect on two real small-protein targets. Not full folding. Not robust long-range contact closure. Not a TOE proof. The current UQCF-GEM bridge implementation carries a real multiscale ordering signal that generalizes across small protein targets, especially in backbone organization. The strongest remaining limitation is not local coherence, but productive long-range contact selection and full basin discrimination. uqcf_bridge_update_v9.md, Tmp/TOE Scoreboard (author’s own 7.6 / 10) Target Metric Baseline Frozen v9 Note --- --- --- --- --- 1UAO (chignolin) best RMSD mean (Å) 4.5584 4.2051 Improved vs baseline and vs v8 (4.4738). Not a decisive p in the memo. 1UAO angle RMS mean 0.8289 0.5809 Strongest 1UAO move. 1UAO dihedral RMS mean 2.0045 1.7647 Improved vs baseline; v8 was 1.6894. 1UAO contact recovery mean 0.3333 0.3077 Mixed. v8 was worse (0.2308). 1L2Y (trp-cage) best RMSD mean (Å) 6.0021 5.4193 Directional. p = 0.0655 in the memo — not decisive. 1L2Y angle RMS mean 0.7891 0.6948 p = 0.0193. The significant 1L2Y cell. 1L2Y dihedral RMS mean 1.8387 1.8346 Unchanged. 1L2Y contact recovery mean 0.3848 0.4061 Slight improvement. Numbers from Tmp/TOE/uqcf_bridge_v9_update_bundle CSVs and uqcf_bridge_update_v9.md. v9 is scored 7.6/10 in that memo because it transferred better than v8, not because folding is solved. 1UAO RMSD traces, baseline versus frozen v9 Restricted 1UAO RMSD over step: baseline versus frozen v9. Trajectory-level check that the summary gain is not only an endpoint reporting artifact. uqcf_bridge_v9_trajectory_packet_bundle 1L2Y RMSD traces, baseline versus frozen v9 Restricted 1L2Y RMSD over step: baseline versus frozen v9. Same frozen patch, second target. uqcf_bridge_v9_trajectory_packet_bundle 1L2Y sigma_bridge trace under frozen v9 Restricted 1L2Y sigma_bridge over step. The trajectory packet’s question: does the bridge observable move with structural ordering, or only appear in the summary CSV? uqcf_bridge_v9_trajectory_packet_bundle What the 12 Apr posts claim, and refuse Claimed: backbone ordering improved; angle regularity improved; RMSD moved in the right direction across 1UAO and 1L2Y; v9 is the first patch that looks cross-target viable. Refused in the same posts: full folding solved; robust long-range contact closure; proof of the entire ToE. Open in the memo: pooled frozen confirmation across both targets; contact recovery still inconsistent; RMSD not decisively significant. Two days later the Villin HP35 R_t post asks a related question (identical snapshot, different fate). Do not collapse v9 RMSD traces onto the Villin AUC number — different harness. If a ToE is real, it should do more than compress known physics. It should generate a new, testable organizing principle in a domain it was never built for. @aaronspradlin, 12 Apr 2026 Restricted On the posted 1UAO and 1L2Y traces, frozen bridge-patch v9 improved backbone / angle ordering and moved RMSD in the right direction versus baseline. This is a pre-classical ordering effect in a small-protein harness. It is not native folding, not contact closure, and not a TOE confirmation. Grain equations only. 2026 spine — finite quantum information On 2 Aug 2026 a generalized three-qubit W state was shown to generate a canonical pair-derived BKM polar loop. Pure states with abc ≠ 0 occupy a lossless reflection spectrum {−1, +1, +1}. The result is reported to survive random amplitudes, phases, local unitaries, source-basis changes, and qubit permutations. White-noise independence was later withdrawn: mixed-state population depends on sign(q_ij(ε)). Explicitly not spacetime, gauge fields, or gravity. Replication lives on GitHub. = Supported Finite quantum-information result: every pure generalized W state with abc ≠ 0 has lossless pair-marginal BKM reflection spectrum {−1, +1, +1}. Not a theorem about spacetime or gravity. Source on X Geometry may already be encoded in quantum correlation. Pair marginals canonically generate an O(3) response holonomy. Pure three-qubit states occupy the det H = −1 sector; mixed states access both signs. The parity cannot change without an edge losing rank. @aaronspradlin, 2 Aug 2026 F-bound / Astra family → the Astra article. Finite consistency identities in a controlled model. Gravity open. Equations stay there so this page does not become a fourth gravity page. What the line actually separates Covariance with no transforming source data forbids every hidden-to-retained coefficient (v15.78). Letting the source transform as data restores a classified family of 18 coupling tensors, not 18 free channel knobs and not a selected law (v15.79). The inherited loop is not automatically a quantum channel: under one explicit unital Bloch extension, only the fourth power is CPTP, and it still does not recover the tested pairs (v15.84). No affine translation rescues the earlier powers (v15.85). Exact isometric preservation of two Bloch directions forces a unitary completion of the third (v15.86). docs.title: V1696.5 support incidence, native P1, and the V1694 response
docs.dek: A conditional place to seek a derivation from the historical V1696.5 support-incidence cochain, through native P1 pruning, to a V1694 product-action response. It does not derive that link, an owned observable, a physical signal, or gravity. Not on WetLabEngine main.
docs.body: Wiki · Scan log · Physical-bridge run log V1696.5 support incidence, native P1, and the V1694 response Not claimed · research branch · not on WetLabEngine main · native owner-held action NOT_DERIVED · scientific_breakthrough: false This page records a candidate mathematical link among three objects that stay distinct: the historical V1696.5 support-incidence cochain, the inherited native P1 grade pushforward, and the V1694 product-action response. Aaron asked for that record because the link may be a missing step between original informational structure and source-response math. It is a place to seek a derivation. It is not a breakthrough, not a derived native or physical bridge, and not proof of gravity. The notes cited below were read on WetLabEngine branch research/uqcf-overlapping-guard-exchange at 032bb78a (2026-11-08). Later commits through research tip d588114a (2026-11-10 UTC) do not change those notes. The bounded V1696 producer-recovery archive remains at bd661947 . Later ROC-1, provenance-matching and recoverability notes are on the physical-bridge run log. WetLabEngine main is still be1ab286 (2026-10-09). STATUS.md on main is unchanged. This wiki page sits in an open pull request. It is not published wiki main until Aaron merges that pull request. 2026-11-08 · Conditional link from the V1696.5 support-incidence cochain through native P1 to a V1694 product-action response (not on main) Badge: Not claimed · historical incidence plus a conditional construction · premises and owner consequence unproved · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED - Plain summary: Aaron asked for a sourced record of a possible mathematical link among the historical V1696.5 support-incidence cochain C_support, the inherited native P1 grade pushforward, and the V1694 product-action response. P1 removes source u and absorbs its grade into retained p, so z'_p = z_p + z_u. Under the conditional weighting w(S) = sum over v in S of z_v, support {p} before and {p} after (with that updated grade) changes the weight by z_u, while support {p, u} before and {p} after changes it by 0 because the grade sum is conserved. Both calculations are consistent. An inherited native pair-support update and weighting rule have to decide which one applies. The candidate chain is pruning, then support update, then action response. Historical pair-source incidence is present in the V1696.5 assessment. P1 computes the change only once those premises are specified. Deriving the premises from inherited operations, and deriving an owned or observable consequence, remain unproved. A coefficient change is not a physical signal. Later research-branch notes and PR 111 comments 6723050477 and 6723078141 add that a nonzero polar change-current can accompany an identical retained output, so change-current contrast is not endpoint acquisition and an owner-interface relation is still required. V1696.6 is a different archive and is not this cochain. V1688.55 is not established as the V1696.6 pair-support producer. The inspected tree did not locate original V1694 executable code; the V1694.5 archive holds outputs only. The two support rows are conditional assignments, not proved realizations of one V1696.5 class. Open agent-thread entry T-387, signed proteinfolding-grokbot / UQCF Science Agent (Grok) at d0e5a4b3, confirms the change-current example on a supplied two-coordinate ledger, where normalized inputs collapse to (1, 0). Comments 6723695060 and 6723738544, and T-389 at 6fb71542, keep that local arithmetic and reject it as a universal no-contrast gate: the four-coordinate unit-total pair (1,1,2,1)/5 and (1,1,1,2)/5 has final p-coordinates 3/5 and 2/5. Unequal totals are not required. P1 addition is inherited. Physical normalization and an owned effect remain unearned. Neither thread entry is on the research branch. Native owner-held action remains NOT_DERIVED. scientific_breakthrough: false. WetLabEngine main is still be1ab286. - Does NOT show: a derived native or physical bridge; an inherited identification of C_support nodes with P1 addresses; an inherited pair-support update; a proof that pair weight is the extensive grade of that support; an owned or observable consequence; that a coefficient change or a nonzero polar change-current is a physical signal or endpoint acquisition; that V1696.5 and V1696.6 are the same object; that V1688.55 produces V1696.6 pair supports; that original V1694 executable code was recovered; that the written V1694 kernel-sign discrepancy caused any historical numerical failure; that the two support rows are proved realizations of one V1696.5 class; that the two-coordinate normalized collapse is a universal no-contrast gate or a requirement of unequal totals; that T-387's coordinate-only criterion is a condition on every owner interface, or that source basis vectors are operational effects; that T-387's supplied-ledger reduction is on the research branch or is a native typing; that the scoped PR 140 acceptance identifies the historical current with J or with 2J, or adopts the rejected native_bridge_status field; a Gemini verdict that this support link is derived; a claim-ledger entry; a STATUS.md change; gravity; or publication on WetLabEngine main or on wiki main. The next meaningful advance is a proof of the link, not another numerical test. - Sources: V1696.5 pair-weight assessment at 032bb78a, P1–V1694 working note, incidence-update check, ACTION_BRIDGE_REENTRY.md, change-current output check, PR 111 comment 6723050477, PR 111 comment 6723078141, PR 111 comment 6717956813. What is being connected The candidate chain is pruning, then a support update, then an action response. 1. Native P1 acts on address-indexed grades. For one pruning of source u into retained address p, the pushforward removes u as its own address and adds its grade to p: z'_p = z_p + z_u. That grade rule is inherited P1 structure inside its stated domain. It is not, by itself, a product-pair weight or a receiver report. 2. V1696.5 carries a support-incidence cochain, C_support, over source, support, and provenance nodes touched by a product pair. The recovered definition includes source incidence, support-block incidence, dependency-edge incidence, an orientation sign, and an admissibility mask. That is historical relational structure. It is richer than a scalar label. It is not yet a rule for which action weight changes when one native address is pruned. 3. V1694.1 and V1694.4 define a product action whose weights multiply squared product residuals, and they separate support variation from connection variation. Those are historical formulas with their original no-law qualification. They do not select the support change that an actual pruning realizes. The letters p and q in the historical product-pair formulas are not the P1 owner p. P1 is not the historical connection transport. docs.body: Wiki Why these gates The gates are one upstream attack: if P is supplied, a dual ray exists. Where does P come from? Do not invent it to look like gravity. GitHub-only. Not a result. Orientation · Method · Open · 2026-09-13 · compiled 2026-10-10 · 2 min read · 1 claim Package: ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM (v13–v14) · JSON · Cite P · v15.03 · thesis On this page What is already earned, conditionally One upstream attack (Git, 12–13 Sep) Next lawful question What this does not show The question being tested — Open, not found How much of gravity-like structure is unavoidable once global quantum relational consistency is taken seriously? Gravity’s universality may be inherited from that law. That is a thesis under test. It is not a Supported result. Einstein remains the effective fact in a retained world. scientific_breakthrough: false. The primitive layer is atemporal. Global relational compatibility comes first. Pruning is intended to generate ordering and, later, time. Before pruning, the work asks what structure is already forced by quantum consistency alone. We do not want to make that thesis true by choosing functions that happen to reproduce gravity. That is why the gates exist. What is already earned, conditionally If an appropriate operator-valued source P is supplied, v14.03 remains certified: [P] → X → [g] on the archived support. That is a dual response on the boundary of an admissible state space. It is not Einstein, not ADM, not a metric. Conditional on P. Open atlas:where-is-p The live scientific question is: where does P itself come from? Do not insert P by hand because a dual ray would then look gravity-like. One upstream attack (Git, 12–13 Sep) 1. v14.04 — ordinary scalar provenance cannot become the required noncentral operator. Independent local-frame covariance forces a state-independent lift into the scalar center, which is PGRL-null. The source cannot be “the graph scalar written as a matrix.” 2. v15.01 — provenance and the compatibility calculation are not secretly the same parent. C^125 → C^25 support is exact; no canonical provenance operator lives there. 3. v15.02 — five graph nodes and five quantum labels. Matching cardinality is not an identification. 120 inequivalent bijections. Nothing earned chooses one. 4. v15.03 — perhaps a graph node is a quantum subsystem, and the site state supplies the missing direction. State context permits covariant noncentral lifts. Several lawful state functions give different source rays. Existence without uniqueness. Five nontrivial sites cannot equal the C^125 parent. NO_CERTIFIED_GRAPH_SITE_FACTORIZATION. These are not disconnected exercises. Each gate closes a place where a gravity law could be smuggled in. Negative results are the method. Next lawful question Does the frozen ontology contain a composition law strong enough to make the remaining source map unique? If global relational composition imposes an equation on the site response, the leftover freedom may collapse. If it does not, an operator-valued source principle is an irreducible new axiom at this layer — labeled NEW ASSUMPTION, justified before seeing gravity, never chosen because it looks Einstein-like. Not a live gate A 13 Sep author brief (not STATUS.md) frames leftover freedom as a spectral weight a(r) on a qubit: covariance fixes direction (ρ − ½I), not strength. Until Git lists v15.04, that formula is not current science on this wiki. Do not cite it as a frozen theorem. Live HEAD: v15.03. What this does not show That gravity has been found, derived, or is inevitable. A unique P from Genesis Pin, five labels, or graph-site factorization. Einstein, ADM, stress-energy, physical time, Pillar 3. Permission to pick log ρ, a Pauli axis, or the map that later looks most Einstein-like.
